battery: Replace batteries with fresh premium alkaline batteries (not cheap brands).
Check battery contacts for corrosion — clean with contact cleaner if needed.
Test voltage under load — electronic locks need ~4.8V+ for 6V systems to fire the solenoid.
Advise customer: replace batteries annually regardless of performance.
If keypad beeps every 10-15 seconds, remove batteries, press each keypad button for 1 second, install fresh Duracell Quantum or Energizer, retry after timeout.
mechanical: Check dial torque with inch-pound gauge — 2+ in-lbs indicates wear.
Reduce handle pressure before entering code to avoid bolt binding.
Listen for grinding when turning dial — indicates bearing wear.
Apply graphite (never oil) to mechanical lock cases.
If handle spins freely without engaging bolts — do not force it, spindle or clutch is broken.
If handle spins freely even before entering code — check setscrew at base of handle, may just be loose.
For combination drift — try combination +1 on each number, then -1. If works, service the dial before closing safe.
Key won't turn — try graphite in keyway. If key is worn, have a duplicate made from original.
environment: Check for signs of rust on bolt slides and hinge area.
Inspect door gap for even spacing — settling can misalign the door.
If in garage/outbuilding, temperature changes can cause expansion issues.
High humidity accelerates corrosion — consider a dehumidifier rod inside the safe.
Ensure safe is on level surface — foundation settling causes door misalignment.
electronic: Lockout mode: wait for timeout period to expire (usually 1-5 minutes), then carefully re-enter code.
Deactivated codes: try any backup codes. If none work, safe may need reprogramming per manufacturer instructions.
Compromised wiring: check keypad cable connection at lock body. Loose connectors can be reseated.
Electronic lock error codes: refer to manufacturer manual for specific blink/beep patterns.
general: Inspect for visible obstructions blocking bolt retraction.
Avoid repeated force attempts — can damage the lock mechanism.
If safe is locked closed and symptoms are progressing, schedule service before a lockout.
Check relock device hasn't accidentally triggered — if triggered, technician required.
Contact a technician if symptoms worsen or you're unsure.
Safe that was dropped or struck may have thrown a relocker — internal inspection required.
Broken linkage (handle turns, bolts don't move) — internal door repair needed, call technician.
If overstuffed, remove items and try opening. Push inward on door while operating handle to relieve bolt pressure.
